src/TutoringCentre.Api/Program.cs: The process composition root registers application and infrastructure services, JSON contracts, telemetry, authentication, and request protections. It selects migrate, seed, and reset-password CLI paths before HTTP execution, then installs the ordered middleware chain and maps all feature endpoint groups. Static files precede explicit routing; trusted forwarded headers run before scheme- and client-dependent behavior. Changes here affect every request and the build-time OpenAPI host.
src/TutoringCentre.Application/Common/Cq: The shared application entry point validates requests, enforces selected-centre and permission markers, resolves typed handlers, and owns command versus query transaction sequencing. Command save can itself return a translated failure, so handler success is provisional. It logs request type and outcome without values. Preserve pre-transaction check order, rollback cleanup, and the prohibition on nested dispatch within one unit of work.
src/TutoringCentre.Infrastructure/Depend: The infrastructure composition method binds runtime and migration database options, registers clocks and interceptor lifetimes, creates the runtime AppDbContext, persists Data Protection keys to PostgreSQL, wires repository/read-service ports, and configures Identity. Runtime DI uses the application connection; migration construction is separate. Interceptor lifetimes differ because audit reads scoped identity while timestamp and tenant guard are stateless.
src/TutoringCentre.Infrastructure/Persis: The adapter begins explicit transactions, sets read-only mode before other SQL for queries, applies a transaction-local current-centre setting, reconciles removed parent links, saves and translates expected persistence failures, then commits or rolls back. Rollback disposes and clears tracking. Its ownership boundary covers handler reads, locks, tracked writes, and generated audit rows.

The single context combines Identity user storage and ordinary domain mappings with the platform Data Protection key context. It reads the actor's centre live, applies assembly configurations, allows a test-model extension, then installs tenant filters last. Only the required DataProtectionKeys DbSet is exposed explicitly; adapters use Set<T> for other types.

The final model convention finds every ITenantOwned mapped type and adds an expression comparing its centre to the context's current actor centre. It rejects owned and keyless tenant mappings. The expression references live context state rather than freezing a centre during model construction; new tenant entities therefore participate without handwritten query predicates.

The save guard rejects changes to existing audit rows and checks every Added, Modified, or Deleted tenant entity against the acting centre. Modified centre properties are forbidden independently of ordinary business edits. It executes after audit generation, so inserted audit entries receive the same ownership check as business rows.

The scoped interceptor snapshots tracked changes, consults explicit audit policy, verifies centre ownership, builds allowed property diffs, and adds audit rows to the same context. It uses one clock instant plus actor and correlation context. Platform bootstrap without a centre is logged rather than audited. Bulk writes that bypass tracking do not receive this behavior.
src/TutoringCentre.Infrastructure/Audit/: The pure diff builder limits output to allowlisted fields and records created, updated, or deleted before/after values. Updated fields require both modification state and real inequality. Phone masking occurs after comparison, avoiding missed changes when masked displays coincide. A null diff means no audit row, and JSON primitive representation is centralized here.
src/TutoringCentre.Infrastructure/Persis: The migration helper emits enable, force, and tenant-isolation policy SQL using the transaction current-centre setting for both row visibility and write checks. It validates table and schema identifiers before interpolation. Policies provide a database backstop independent of EF filters, so runtime privileges and transaction-local settings remain essential.

The shared mapping establishes required centre ownership, a Restrict reference to platform.centres, and a composite alternate key on centre and entity ID. Child composite foreign keys can then prove both existence and same-centre ownership. A plain unique index is insufficient as the principal key target used by EF relationship mapping.

The mapping exposes PostgreSQL xmin through the shadow uint property Version, generated on add or update and used as an EF concurrency token. Domain entities need no PostgreSQL-specific field. Versioned adapters must set the client's value as OriginalValue so EF rejects stale updates at save rather than merely trusting a loaded row.

The translator distinguishes optimistic concurrency, unique constraint, and exclusion constraint failures using types, SQLSTATE, and constraint names. Known normal conflicts become Results; deliberately excluded invariants and other database faults remain exceptions. Unknown unique names receive a generic conflict plus warning, while unknown exclusion names remain loud.

The catalogue binds exact database constraint names to public feature errors and field details. It explicitly excludes one-primary-parent and rule/date duplicate constraints because those indicate application invariant failures. Adding or renaming a migration constraint requires reviewing this contract so race losers and friendly pre-checks retain consistent outcomes.
src/TutoringCentre.Api/Auth/AuthEndpoint: Transport orchestration handles antiforgery token issue, credentials, ticket creation, logout, profile, centre selection, and password change through application ports. Login suppresses auto-selection when password replacement is pending; password change issues a new centreless ticket. Identity and membership rules live behind ports rather than direct infrastructure dependencies.
src/TutoringCentre.Api/Auth/Authenticati: The setup configures the secure HttpOnly host-prefixed session cookie, eight-hour sliding ticket lifetime, per-request validation hook, API-style 401/403 behavior, and authenticated fallback policy. Cache options are bound here; database key persistence is registered in Infrastructure. Cookie setting changes must respect browser prefix rules and existing client behavior.
src/TutoringCentre.Api/Auth/SessionReval: The cookie validation hook reads user, stamp, selected centre, and role before an Application actor exists. It caches positive query results by that tuple, rejects invalid principals, and clears invalid cookies. Role freshness now participates alongside stamp and membership activity. The positive cache creates a bounded delay rather than instant revocation.
src/TutoringCentre.Api/Auth/ActorMiddlew: This is the HTTP claims-to-Application identity translation point. It builds a staff actor only from a parseable user ID and a valid centre/role pairing, leaves malformed sessions without a trusted actor, and invokes the next middleware. Handlers consume ICurrentActor rather than parsing claims independently.
src/TutoringCentre.Infrastructure/Identi: The credential adapter uses UserManager for account lookup, dummy verification for unknown email, lockout, password checking, and failure counters. Password change rejects reuse, maps mismatch and policy errors, clears pending replacement, and updates security stamp. Its existence does not establish measured timing equality or cancellation coverage for UserManager calls.

The provisioning adapter reuses an existing login unchanged or generates a cryptographic temporary password and creates a pending-change account. UserManager uses the same scoped context, so creation inside dispatch participates in its transaction. Existing accounts return no temporary password; new plaintext credentials are returned for the creation response rather than stored as a user field.
src/TutoringCentre.Application/Staff/Com: The handler ensures a login, refuses any existing membership in the acting centre, constructs an active membership, and returns IDs plus a temporary password only when applicable. One dispatch transaction covers account and membership. A pre-existing inactive membership requires reactivation rather than a duplicate create operation.

Role mutation loads the target inside the acting centre, refuses self-change, locks/counts active owners only for an active owner demotion, then invokes the domain transition. The ordered checks protect the last owner and avoid revealing foreign membership state. It changes a per-centre membership, never a global login role.

Deactivation follows scoped load, self protection, conditional last-owner locking, and Membership.Deactivate. It retains the row and leaves the login account and other-centre memberships intact. Session revalidation subsequently observes inactive membership subject to its positive cache duration.
src/TutoringCentre.Infrastructure/Identi: The scoped provider converts actor identity into All, Own, or None group ownership scope and caches that decision once per request. Teacher roles resolve through an active linked academic teacher; missing linkage fails closed. System and unrestricted staff roles get All while unknown actors never default to unrestricted data.
src/TutoringCentre.Domain/Identity/RoleP: The central matrix maps per-centre staff roles to capability strings for subjects, students, teachers, groups, enrollments, schedule, staff, audit, and settings. Dispatcher authorization and profile permission projection use this map. Unknown roles and keys deny access; frontend visibility is a presentation of this server policy, not its enforcement.
src/TutoringCentre.Domain/Common/PhoneNu: The immutable value object canonicalizes supported phone spellings into E.164, including selected Egyptian local forms and Arabic digit sets, then compares by canonical value. Masked output retains a prefix and suffix for privacy, separately from equality. Preserve conversion rules when changing uniqueness or audit representation.
src/TutoringCentre.Domain/Common/SearchT: The matching normalizer trims and collapses whitespace, lowercases, removes selected Arabic diacritics and tatweel, maps Arabic letter variants, and converts Arabic digit sets. Display values are kept separately. Stored fields and search terms must use compatible normalization; changing this algorithm may require persisted-value backfills.
src/TutoringCentre.Domain/Academics/Stud: The student aggregate owns its parent links and enforces one-to-four contacts, no duplicates, and exactly one primary. Successful link changes increase LinksRevision; archived students are read-only for ordinary edits. Registration creates a primary link immediately, and primary replacement is a dedicated atomic in-memory transition.
src/TutoringCentre.Application/Academics: Registration resolves an existing parent or constructs a new canonical-phone parent, then constructs the student and primary link within one dispatch transaction. A newly tracked parent remains provisional if later student validation fails. Nested parent dispatch is deliberately avoided so both aggregates share one save and rollback boundary.
src/TutoringCentre.Domain/Academics/Teac: The teaching record is separate from the login account, with an optional UserId link, canonical optional phone, normalized search name, and archive lifecycle. Link/unlink are domain transitions; eligibility belongs to the handler's staff-directory contract. Archiving preserves the account link and historical identity.
src/TutoringCentre.Application/Academics: The handler loads a versioned teacher, unlinks for null input, or checks an active Teacher-role membership through IStaffDirectory before linking. It rejects account reuse through both a pre-check and database unique constraint. Equivalent eligibility refusals avoid disclosing whether a supplied user is unknown, foreign, inactive, or the wrong role.
src/TutoringCentre.Domain/Academics/Grou: A group keeps centre and subject fixed while allowing bounded capacity, name, teacher, and archive transitions. Capacity decisions receive a repository-supplied active count rather than storing a duplicate counter. EnsureCanEnroll rejects archived or full groups; callers must obtain the correct lock before supplying the count.
src/TutoringCentre.Infrastructure/Reposi: The write adapter loads versioned groups and provides the lock-and-count enrollment operation. Its parameterized FOR UPDATE query names xmin explicitly, then counts active enrollments only after the row lock is held. This operation is shared by enrollment, capacity shrink, and archive to serialize the relevant decision window.
src/TutoringCentre.Domain/Academics/Enro: An enrollment records a fixed student and group relationship with start time, then can end once with a reason and valid end instant. Transfer does not mutate GroupId or reactivate history; it ends one row and starts another. External state such as capacity and duplicate active seats is checked by handlers and database constraints.
src/TutoringCentre.Application/Academics: Creation locks the group and counts seats before resolving the student, checking active state and duplicates, applying the capacity rule, and tracking a new enrollment. The ordering gives foreign groups a consistent not-found result and serializes competing seat decisions. The clock supplies the start instant explicitly.

Transfer loads the versioned active source, rejects the same destination, locks only target capacity, requires a matching subject, and checks duplicate/capacity rules. One timestamp ends the source as Transferred and starts the destination. Only the destination needs a capacity lock, avoiding opposing-transfer lock cycles.
src/TutoringCentre.Domain/Academics/Sche: The recurrence entity stores local weekday, five-minute-boundary start, bounded stepped duration, room, and effective dates. It carries no teacher, offset, or instant; those come from group and centre context during generation. Rules end once rather than editing recurrence history in place.

The pure generator evaluates each local date separately, applies explicit skipped/repeated DST policy, converts to UTC, and adds duration as elapsed minutes. It accepts zone and range explicitly and reads no clock or repository. Repeated UTC additions would break its wall-clock recurrence contract across offset changes.

A dated occurrence stores UTC instants, original local date, rule and group identity, room, and teacher snapshot. Its internal factory restricts creation to generation. Cancellation requires a future scheduled session, while reassignment only changes future scheduled occurrences and leaves started or cancelled history untouched.
src/TutoringCentre.Infrastructure/Reposi: The adapter tracks versioned sessions, projects existing generation dates, loads future or later scheduled occurrences, and takes sorted transaction-scoped advisory teacher locks. It avoids bulk updates because tracking drives auditing and tenant write guards. Existing rule dates provide generation idempotency independently of cancellation status.
src/TutoringCentre.Application/Academics: The handler resolves an active group and centre zone, calculates centre-local today, bounds effective-from, builds the rule, takes a teacher schedule lock, and tracks the initial 28-day generation. It does not perform an overlap pre-check; exclusion constraints decide at save and rollback the entire rule batch on conflict.

Extension resolves active rules and their current group teachers, bounds the requested date, locks every affected teacher, and generates only missing rule/date occurrences. The whole centre action shares one transaction, so one overlap prevents partial extension. Existing local dates are the idempotency identity.

Ending a versioned rule sets its inclusive final local date and cancels later still-future scheduled sessions in the same transaction. No row is deleted and no generation occurs. Each tracked cancellation participates in concurrency, audit, and tenant checks.

Reassignment validates a visible active teacher, locks old and new teacher schedules, changes the versioned group, and moves future scheduled sessions as tracked entities. Past and cancelled sessions retain history. Any new-teacher overlap rejects the common save and restores group and sessions together.
src/TutoringCentre.Infrastructure/ReadSe: Schedule reads apply tenant isolation plus explicit teacher ownership in SQL. Rule visibility follows a group's current teacher, while timetable visibility follows each session's stored teacher. Week filtering uses stored local dates, preserving early-morning Cairo sessions whose UTC date is the previous day.

The list adapter applies archive/search/cursor criteria, retrieves one extra ordered row, then loads primary-parent data for page IDs. Name matching executes through normalized escaped LIKE; phone-fragment matching intentionally materializes tenant-scoped phone projections because the value conversion prevented the attempted SQL translation. Its memory work has a documented scale limit.

Audit reads apply filters and descending occurrence-plus-ID keyset paging, left join only actor display names, and convert stored JSON changes into DTO values. One extra row determines the next cursor. The adapter preserves audit rows without a current actor-user match and does not return actor email.
src/TutoringCentre.Api/Http/ResultHttpEx: The shared transport mapper converts result kinds to status and Problem Details while preserving field dictionaries for any kind, including conflicts. Creation helpers support both Location-bearing and body-only 201 contracts. Feature endpoints choose the success shape; they do not duplicate failure switches.
src/TutoringCentre.Infrastructure/Persis: Migration application requires a separate owner connection and constructs a short-lived anonymous context outside runtime DI. It applies pending schema changes and disposes that context. Its summary caller list is stale because MigrateCommand now invokes it in addition to development startup and seeding.
src/TutoringCentre.Api/Cli/ResetPassword: The operator-only command creates an Identity scope, finds the requested account, removes its old password, then attempts to add the new password and returns an exit code. There is no explicit transaction around removal and addition in the inspected method; a rejected new password can therefore leave the old password already removed. Treat this ordering as an operational risk rather than a generic atomic reset promise.
src/TutoringCentre.Infrastructure/ReadSe: Projects settings and the xmin-backed client version without tracking. Centre rows deliberately have neither tenant query filters nor RLS, so its supplied centre ID is the security boundary; callers must take that ID from the actor rather than untrusted request input.

Builds active group rosters and a student enrollment history through tenant-filtered joins. TeacherScope filters the group before reading a roster; a nonexistent student returns null, whereas a valid student with no permitted groups yields an empty list. The roster cap equals the domain maximum capacity and assumes the write invariant remains intact.

Applies archive, subject, teacher, and teacher-ownership predicates before a capped SQL projection. Joins supply subject and teacher names; an active-enrollment correlated count supplies occupancy without a denormalized counter. Unknown or missing Own scope fails closed without querying groups.

Reads profile, memberships, active-centre membership, password gate, and cookie session state. These identity rows are globally readable by the runtime role, so each operation explicitly filters the requested user. Session state includes the current role as well as security stamp and membership activity, allowing stale role claims to be rejected.

Reads parent details and exact canonical-phone matches without tracking. The children query joins filtered links to filtered students, orders by name, and caps children at fifty. Phone value objects are converted to output strings after materialization to avoid unsupported SQL member translation.

Lists centre memberships joined to user display name and email, including role, status, version, and the self marker. Membership has no implicit tenant protection, so the explicit centre predicate is mandatory. The application permission check protects this staff-specific exposure of email.

Projects subject IDs, names, status, and xmin versions with no tracking. Entity filters run before projection; the list excludes archived subjects by default, sorts names, and caps results at five hundred. The cap is truncation rather than cursor pagination.

Translates EF applied and pending migration metadata into the application SchemaStatus record. It returns the last applied migration and pending count, preventing EF migration types from leaking through the application port.

Reads teachers with optional linked-account display names through a left join and computes active group counts. It deliberately exposes no linked-account email. List results are capped at five hundred, while user-to-teacher resolution requires an active teacher so archived records cannot obtain Own read scope.
src/TutoringCentre.Infrastructure/Reposi: Tracks platform centres, checks slug uniqueness, and sets the caller version as EF OriginalValue for subsequent optimistic UPDATE checks. It contains no save call: dispatcher-owned UnitOfWork controls persistence and audit. Centre scoping remains the handler responsibility because this platform entity has no tenant filter.

Tracks explicitly centre-filtered memberships and installs expected xmin versions. Its active-owner locking query uses parameterized ADO.NET, joins the current EF transaction, reads FOR UPDATE rows, and counts them in memory because PostgreSQL cannot combine that locking clause with COUNT. This serialization supports last-owner protections.

Tracks parent roots, sets expected xmin on mutation loads, supports exact PhoneNumber equality lookup, and excludes a chosen root during duplicate-phone checks. Add only enrolls a row in tracking; unique constraints and UnitOfWork determine the final write outcome.

Tracks rules and expected xmin versions. Active-rule enumeration includes only active groups and rules whose inclusive end has not passed the requested date, ordered by group, weekday, and start time. The group check asks whether any rule has not ended as of today rather than whether it has already begun.

Always eagerly loads parent links for both mutation and ordinary tracked lookup, preserving aggregate collection invariants during unlink and primary-parent operations. Mutation lookup also sets the client xmin OriginalValue. Omitting Include would make valid links appear absent to the aggregate.

Provides tracked subject lookup, normalized-name duplicate checks excluding a supplied entity, and deferred insertion. Mutation lookup places the client version in EF OriginalValue; a stale write is detected by the eventual database UPDATE rather than an early in-memory comparison.

Provides tracked teacher loads, expected xmin assignment, account-link uniqueness checks excluding the current teacher, and deferred insertion. Its account check is tenant-filtered through the entity query filter; eligibility of the identity account belongs to the application staff-directory port.
src/TutoringCentre.Infrastructure/Time/S: Adapts TimeProvider UTC time and the host TimeZoneInfo database to IClock. General FromLocal obtains the zone offset and normalizes to UTC; recurrence generation has its own explicit ambiguous/invalid-time policy, so this utility should not be mistaken for the scheduling DST algorithm.
src/TutoringCentre.Infrastructure/Persis: Checks the actual PostgreSQL current_user for superuser, BYPASSRLS, or schema-owner identity and fails readiness with a generic description if any applies. It detects dangerous connection-string configuration independently of whether ordinary connectivity succeeds. Database exceptions flow to health-check handling.

Emits schema USAGE and owner-specific default privileges for future tables, granting SELECT, INSERT, and UPDATE. Existing tables still need explicit grants and DELETE requires a deliberate exception. Reversal removes both default privileges and schema usage, so schema-sharing migration order matters.

Provides a narrower schema/default/table grant protocol for append-only data: SELECT and INSERT only. Audit immutability depends on runtime privileges lacking UPDATE and DELETE in addition to application behavior. The reverse operation revokes table grants, future defaults, and schema usage.

Signals a tenant write-guard rejection and identifies the CLR entity type for internal diagnostics. It is intentionally not a business Result: uncaught guard violations reach the generic HTTP exception path, because they indicate a programming or isolation failure.
src/TutoringCentre.Application/Academics: Loads a versioned student, refuses archival while active enrollments exist, then asks the aggregate to archive. The enrollment existence check is a cross-aggregate business precondition; the repository and UnitOfWork still own tenant scoping and optimistic persistence.

Loads a versioned teacher and refuses archival when active teaching groups remain. Archival changes business availability while retaining the optional account association and historical references. Staff membership lifecycle is separate.

Prevents subject archival while an active group references it, then delegates the state transition to Subject. This check preserves usable group dependencies without deleting either group or subject history.

Revalidates the referenced subject and teacher before restoring an archived group. Existing foreign keys establish existence and centre consistency, while these application checks require current active business state. Restoring a row therefore cannot silently revive a group with archived dependencies.

Constructs the canonical phone value object and asks the parent read service for an exact match. Absence is a successful null response rather than NotFound, supporting optional reuse in student registration. The endpoint uses a POST body to keep phone values out of URL paths and query strings.

Loads the student with the supplied version and applies the aggregate update to name and optional contact fields. This is a replacement-style operation: absent optional values clear them. Phone parsing and domain validation precede final UnitOfWork save.

Loads a versioned teacher and replaces editable personal fields through domain validation. Optional phone removal is intentional, while account linkage is handled by a separate command with identity eligibility checks. Successful handler return remains provisional until persistence succeeds.
src/TutoringCentre.Application/Audit/Aud: Encodes the descending audit keyset position as timestamp ticks plus event ID, transported as an opaque Base64 token. Decoding checks token structure and numeric/GUID parsing, but DateTimeOffset construction can throw for out-of-range ticks; callers should not assume every malformed token returns false.
